current_text: Every table out there has its plate. The tray stands empty by the counter until tomorrow's service.
Lyonette sets the cloth down and stops counting cutlery. Most people talk straight past me. Sit where you like — I'll bring something hot.
[Advanced Cooking] — Vegetables browned, stew reduced until a spoon stands up in it, bread out of the cloth warm. The fine meal goes out on a plate wiped clean at the rim.
The copper pan hangs above the range on its own hook, scoured bright. It comes down for a signature dish and nothing less.
One pot of stock and three plates called for. Stretching the one across the three is a cook's trick, and you have not got it.
Six planks, one strap hinge, a latch worn pale on the thumb side. The bottom edge is warped, and the draught under it comes through smelling of onions.
[Detect Magic] — The frame reads as warding, layer over layer, the deepest of it older than the paint above it. All of it is live, and it is keyed to the cellar side of the door.
Coat off and folded over the chair back, sleeves turned up past the elbow. He keeps one palm flat on the door's face, and his other hand taps a count against his thigh.
Scratching behind the pantry wall, down low at the level of the skirting board. It stops when you hold still and starts again when you move.
Rings, crumbs, and a smear of gravy going tacky on the boards. One good wipe-down clears the lot.
Dry wick, trimmed, and the glass wiped clean. An orb of cold light would sit in there as well as any flame.
The best bedding in the house is on this bed: thick sheets under a wool blanket, and a pillow that holds its shape.
Narrow desk under the window, one drawer. A pale cup-ring in the varnish.
You have nothing yet to put on it. Dust lifts off the front lip when you set your hand down.
Nothing there. Bare plaster and floorboards, with a thin draught coming off the window frame.
The mattress has fresh straw in it and the blanket has been beaten out. It smells of soap and nothing else.
Thick bedding now, and a shutter that latches shut. The wind off the floodplains stops at the window.
Your arm is done for today. The shafts are out of the straw and back in the quiver.
The shaft goes into the straw and stands there. You walk down and pull it out for the next draw.
Nothing there. Bare stone, and a rack of spare kit with every strap buckled the same way.

A SCRAP OF PARCHMENT, tacked low and half hidden under the notice above it. 'LOST: one backup warhammer, plain steel, no love lost between us but I want it back. Ask for Renn. Reward for the honest sort.' The bottom line runs downhill off the edge of the paper.
A card tacked to the board's top rail, ruled and lettered by hand: rates set by the Guild, complaints to the Guildmistress in person. The initials in the corner are S.S.

Handbills pinned onto the plaster, the outer ones lapping over the request board's edge. One offers a reward for a plain steel warhammer; half a card under it advertises a back room to let, quiet tenants only.

The smaller board carries lost gear, rooms going spare, and one duel challenge with nothing written under it. Anything worth chasing copies into your journal as a lead: a name and a place, nothing promised.
Nothing there. The floorboard in front of the desk is walked pale, chalk dust in the grain.
A line chalked on the rail under the board: start with the market run. The slips above it pay more and go further.
THE DELIVERY BOARD, in painted letters at the top. Gold by distance, paid on the mark, same-waking terms; take a slip at the counter.
Inside a wide stone hearth swept down to the brick: split kindling, dry birch laid over it in a lattice. Cold air comes down the flue and stirs the loose bark.
[Basic Cleaning] — The dried mud comes off in flakes under the cloth. The grain shows pale, and the road smell goes with it.
Nothing there. Blank slips under a stone weight, and a block of rope wax with a thumb-groove worn into it.
Fur brushed flat at the shoulder where a strap sits, ears up and turning at every voice in the row. She looks at your boots and your hands before your face, and she does not hurry about it.
The guard's eyes leave the road for a moment and settle on you. Hah. You'll do. Go on through, and I'll know your face next time.

Olesm brightens like a lamp. Oh! A friendly face. Most people's eyes glaze when I mention troop dispersal. Yours didn't. Would you — that is — care to see the board sometime? No pressure. A little pressure.
Round loaves stacked four high, the top ones still steaming through their cloth. The chalk board carries today's price, and a higher one under it for after the fourth bell.
A card propped against the near stack warns that the seller remembers faces. Silverfang goods: cheap tin and cord at the front edge, bolts of plains wool set back behind them.
The Gnoll who keeps the stall is working a price upward, and the card on the cloth says she remembers faces and debts. Silverfang goods at honest prices, cheapest to the front.
The plains-wool bolt you carried up stands at eye level on the near stand, cut into and already half gone by the yard. A customer has the end of it in both hands, arguing the price down.
